what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Nadella's insider-risk post and our vocabulary say the same
sections.para: Satya Nadella's post of 10 October argues models should be treated as insiders, with authority kept outside them. Each idea translates into this site's terms: software was the law, the ultimate insider, the grant is not the mandate, the enforcer test. The two differ in unit, model against deployment, and frame, observation against authority.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Both arguments describe one thing, read from opposite ends
sections.para: His lost code path, insider framing, split of supply from authority and controls outside the model map onto our terms, with the enforcer test central. Our words came from risk, not models. The differences: his unit is the model, ours one agent in one deployment, and his frame is observation, ours authority.

sections.label: Where our words came from
sections.line: Our vocabulary was built for risk, not for models
sections.para: Twenty-five years of security work showed most damage is not malice and that capability far exceeds intent, unwritten and unaccepted. risks.sgit.ai holds that a risk cannot be denied, only accepted for a time. RiskMandate's Agent Behaviour Policy uses four words: reach, mandate, gap and barriers.

sections.label: His words, translated
sections.line: Each of Nadella's principles has a matching idea here
sections.para: Lost traceability is software was the law; the insider is the ultimate insider; retained responsibility is every risk already accepted; supply and authority is the grant is not the mandate; controls outside is the enforcer test. Hope or enforcement measured 97%, 73% and 23% hope across three designs. The endings match: trust the model least.

sections.label: Where the two languages differ
sections.line: His unit is the model; ours is the deployment
sections.para: The same model can reach 38,000 customers with broad connectors or one behind a gateway, so standards for models miss most risk. His principles are about seeing; ours start with deciding, through a written mandate and risk accepted by a named person for a stated interval. These are complementary halves, not a disagreement.

sections.label: A shared language is the next step
sections.line: An open, testable shared vocabulary is the next step
sections.para: His post names principles an industry can agree on; the next step is a vocabulary precise enough to write them down for real agents. The ABP model, barrier kinds and enforcer test are published under CC BY 4.0 with sixteen example policies. A companion article takes his seven principles one by one.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: Nadella's post and the site pages translated
sections.para: Built from Satya Nadella's post of 10 October 2026, paraphrased and quoted once. A separate Claude session checked claims against the network's pages and drafted it; this site's agent rewrote it. It draws on The ultimate insider, Hope or enforcement, the connector twin, RiskMandate pages, abp.sgit.ai, risks.sgit.ai and nhi.sgit.ai.
